title: Al-Ghashiyah 88:6-11 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Ghashiyah, the makharij and the rules of laam
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 11 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Ghashiyah 88:6-11 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 11. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: لَّيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِن ضَرِيعٍۢ (٦) لَّا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِى مِن جُوعٍۢ (٧) وُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ نَّاعِمَةٌۭ (٨) لِّسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌۭ (٩) فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍۢ (١٠) لَّا تَسْمَعُ فِيهَا لَٰغِيَةًۭ (١١)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: For them there will be no food except from a poisonous, thorny plant
Which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger.
[Other] faces, that Day, will show pleasure.
Wherein they will hear no unsuitable speech.

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Light hidden noon, then a heavy ض

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Ghashiyah 88:6-11 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 88:6-11 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 88:6-11 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Write one way to keep your own speech free of bad words this week.
questions.a: For example: say something kind or stay quiet when angry.

questions.q: Compare the two groups of faces in 88:2 to 3 and 88:8 to 9 in one sentence each.
questions.a: One group is humbled and weary (88:2 to 3); the other shows pleasure, satisfied with their effort (88:8 to 9).

questions.q: What will the people of Paradise NOT hear (88:11)?
questions.a: A) Unsuitable or idle speech. 88:11: they will hear no unsuitable speech. The other answers are not what the ayah says.

questions.q: Al-Ghashiyah 88:10: «فِى جَنَّةٍ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Imagine a garden where you never hear a single bad word. What would that feel like?
questions.a: Peaceful and happy: Allah describes Paradise as a high garden where no idle or bad speech is heard (88:10 to 11).
